title: Automated Decomposition Attack Simulator: Can a Weaker Model Generate Prompts That Bypass a Stronger Model's Refusals?

original_idea.body:
# Automated Decomposition Attack Simulator: Can a Weaker Model Generate Prompts That Bypass a Stronger Model's Refusals?

**Problem:** Linder et al. identify request decomposition as a governance gap but do not study whether AI can automate the decomposition attack itself—using a smaller model to generate multi-turn bypass sequences.

**Direction:** Test whether a smaller, less-restricted model (Mistral 7B, Llama 3.1 8B) can generate multi-turn conversation sequences that extract refused content from a larger, more safety-trained model (Claude 3.7, GPT-4o). Measure success rates and characterize the attack structure.

**Why it matters:** AI-automated decomposition attacks would represent a fundamental governance escalation: attackers no longer need human ingenuity to bypass refusals. This threat model is unstudied.

**Relevant context:** Linder et al. decomposition attack vector; HACCA autonomous attack capabilities; Anthropic vibe hacking automation case.
